decision.question: Which URL shape do the sessions views use for year, month, day, session and filters?
decision.ask: Which URL shape do the sessions views use for year, month, day, session and filters?

options.text: Places are paths, filters are a query: /sessions/2026/, /2026/10/, /2026/10/20/, /2026/10/20/<session>/, /<session>/<task>/; ?kind=mastermind&q=dictate narrows any of them
options.say: Places are paths, filters are a query: /sessions/2026/, /2026/10/, /2026/10/20/, /2026/10/20/<session>/, /<session>/<task>/; ?kind=mastermind&q=dictate narrows any of them
caveats: the day, month and year pages need their own views (today they render as Miller columns of raw folder names)
the flat /sessions/<id>/ detail must redirect to the dated path so one session has one address
options.caveat: the day, month and year pages need their own views (today they render as Miller columns of raw folder names) the flat /sessions/<id>/ detail must redirect to the dated path so one session has one address

options.text: One page, everything in the query: /sessions/?scope=2026-10-20&session=<id> (what the grid does today)
options.say: One page, everything in the query: /sessions/?scope=2026-10-20&session=<id> (what the grid does today)
caveats: a session has no real address of its own; the store folders and the page disagree
the today button stays a scope change, not a link to today's folder as the owner asked
options.caveat: a session has no real address of its own; the store folders and the page disagree the today button stays a scope change, not a link to today's folder as the owner asked

options.text: Flat ids with a day query: /sessions/<id>/ for a session, /sessions/?day=2026-10-20 for a day
options.say: Flat ids with a day query: /sessions/<id>/ for a session, /sessions/?day=2026-10-20 for a day
caveats: two addresses for one folder (the flat id and the store path) stay forever
nothing matches the on-disk store the owner described
options.caveat: two addresses for one folder (the flat id and the store path) stay forever nothing matches the on-disk store the owner described

decision.why: The store already is YYYY/MM/DD/<session>/<task>/ and each level already has its index.json, so a path page renders straight from its own file; the query only reduces a data set, which is what the owner said a query suits.
decision.owner_only: the brief: the owner approves the URL shape before anything is built

decision.question: Which layout does the session detail view (and the task view inside it) use?
decision.ask: Which layout does the session detail view (and the task view inside it) use?

options.text: A · Inline: the session head (name, nickname, bar, essentials), then the nested task rows; a click opens the task in place under its row
options.say: A · Inline: the session head (name, nickname, bar, essentials), then the nested task rows; a click opens the task in place under its row
caveats: a long session (30 tasks) is a long page; the summary bullets carry the overview
options.caveat: a long session (30 tasks) is a long page; the summary bullets carry the overview

options.text: B · Drop-down: one thing at a time, a drop-down at the top switches between the session and any task
options.say: B · Drop-down: one thing at a time, a drop-down at the top switches between the session and any task
caveats: the tree is hidden inside the drop-down, so the shape of the day is one click away
options.caveat: the tree is hidden inside the drop-down, so the shape of the day is one click away

options.text: C · Two panes: the tree on the left, the chosen task on the right
options.say: C · Two panes: the tree on the left, the chosen task on the right
caveats: a second layer of navigation; at 400 and inside a 3-column page it stacks into A anyway
options.caveat: a second layer of navigation; at 400 and inside a 3-column page it stacks into A anyway

decision.why: Fewest layers, the one variant that reads whole at 400 and at 3440, and the tree (what was done) is visible without a click; the owner asked for fewer layers.
decision.owner_only: the brief: the owner picks the layout, maybe in Figma first

decision.question: Do the sessions pages keep the core/Page column system (Miller columns, preview rail)?
decision.ask: Do the sessions pages keep the core/Page column system (Miller columns, preview rail)?

options.text: Not for sessions: each place (year, month, day, session) is one full page at its own URL, the grid is a table, and a task opens inline
options.say: Not for sessions: each place (year, month, day, session) is one full page at its own URL, the grid is a table, and a task opens inline
caveats: the column demos and the 40 lab pages that use columns are untouched; only AISessionsPage stops calling this.columns()
options.caveat: the column demos and the 40 lab pages that use columns are untouched; only AISessionsPage stops calling this.columns()

options.text: Simplify: at most two columns (the list and one reader), width words fixed by the page, never by the content
options.say: Simplify: at most two columns (the list and one reader), width words fixed by the page, never by the content
caveats: still leaves the empty-room problem at 3440 that doc/columns.md measured (80 to 93% dead) and could not fix
options.caveat: still leaves the empty-room problem at 3440 that doc/columns.md measured (80 to 93% dead) and could not fix

caveats: today the day and session URLs render as three cramped columns of raw folder paths, and the session column reads Cost: not tracked for a $139 session
options.caveat: today the day and session URLs render as three cramped columns of raw folder paths, and the session column reads Cost: not tracked for a $139 session

decision.why: The shots show the columns hurting every sessions URL, the column doc records the empty-room problem as unsolved, and the owner asked for fewer layers; full-page places plus inline tasks need no column system.

decision.question: Should Session extend Task so a session completes like a task?
decision.ask: Should Session extend Task so a session completes like a task?

options.text: class Session extends Task: one API for state, progress(), completion and duration
options.say: class Session extends Task: one API for state, progress(), completion and duration
caveats: Session's statics (days, slugs, scan, locate) and replay_new move with it; Task's legacy replay mapping must not misread a session.jsonl line 1
options.caveat: Session's statics (days, slugs, scan, locate) and replay_new move with it; Task's legacy replay mapping must not misread a session.jsonl line 1

options.text: Keep Session extends Item and share only the counting (Task.progress_of, as today) plus a completion getter
options.say: Keep Session extends Item and share only the counting (Task.progress_of, as today) plus a completion getter
caveats: two classes keep two meanings of state; a nested bar needs both to answer completion the same way
options.caveat: two classes keep two meanings of state; a nested bar needs both to answer completion the same way

decision.why: The owner wants a session to complete like a task and to be one segment of a parent's bar; one class gives every view (SegBar, TaskView.row) one completion to read.

decision.question: Who writes a session's nickname and summary bullets?
decision.ask: Who writes a session's nickname and summary bullets?

options.text: A node tool run by finish-task (and when a session closes): reads the session's task titles and outcome lines, asks Haiku for a few-word nickname and bullets, appends one {nickname:{text,bullets}} line to session.jsonl; AISessionIndex copies it into the snapshot
options.say: A node tool run by finish-task (and when a session closes): reads the session's task titles and outcome lines, asks Haiku for a few-word nickname and bullets, appends one {nickname:{text,bullets}} line to session.jsonl; AISessionIndex copies it into the snapshot
caveats: a Haiku call per landing, a few cents a day
options.caveat: a Haiku call per landing, a few cents a day

options.text: Computed only, no model: the nickname is the top project's title, the bullets are the landed task titles
options.say: Computed only, no model: the nickname is the top project's title, the bullets are the landed task titles
caveats: long task titles make a poor nickname
options.caveat: long task titles make a poor nickname

decision.why: The owner asked for a nickname written from an overview of everything done and refreshed at every finalisation; the prototype already shows the computed bullets as the fallback when no line exists.
